title: The V1 session is played through on an emulated 390x844 touch phone, and the chrome it broke is rebuilt into bands
context: The owner's friends open the live link on phones, and nothing built in the two days before this — the sector line, the views strip, the gunship seat, SOL-82's seat, the MK-9, the in-game debrief, SKIP TUTORIAL — had been touched by a thumb. The mobile shell existed and was ruled for a landscape about 844x303; a portrait 390x844 phone had never been walked end to end, and the shell answered portrait with a full-screen 'rotate your phone' wall, which is a closed door for a friend who just opened a link.
outcome: A --phone step in scripts/browser-test.mjs emulates the phone before the page boots (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride 390x844 dpr 3 mobile, setTouchEmulationEnabled, and pointer/hover coarse via setEmulatedMedia, so the shell's (pointer: coarse) query is true at module load) and plays the V1 session with Input.dispatchTouchEvent only: the bare opening, SKIP TUTORIAL tapped into the skipped run, the pad and strip and sector line and comms card, driving on the stick that appears under the finger, a tower ordered by tap through BUILD, the gunship seat from the strip with its guns by touch and the pad's fire button as the trigger, the MK-9 painted and released by two taps, SOL-82's scope steered by a drag and burned by holding HOLD, the five-page debrief advanced by tap to CONTINUE, and the same chrome at 844x390. At every station each control must be 44 px and document.elementFromPoint at its centre must find the control itself, and in portrait no two pieces of chrome may share more than a 2 px sliver. Portrait plays: the rotate wall becomes a passive hint that fades, and the chrome is laid out in bands — a top row for the shell's bar and the mode switch, the HUD and the radar under it, the announcement row with the SKIP offer at its right, a full-width row for the coach, the sector brief, then the play area, Isao's card, the strip and the pad. The seats keep the pad's fire button as their trigger and hide BUILD; the strip's MAP is dropped on a phone because BUILD already is the orbit view and the seats carry their own map button.
alternatives: Leaving the portrait rotate wall and testing landscape only: rejected — the link is opened one-handed and upright, and a wall is a closed door.

Holding landscape to portrait's rule that no two pieces of chrome touch at all: dropped. At 844x390 the bottom lane cannot hold both Isao's card and the views strip, and the read-only captions still stack. The strip moved to the free middle of the top row and landscape is now held to the contract that matters — every control reachable at 44 px and no control under another — with the caption stacking recorded rather than papered over.
Duplicating a seat switch on the pad: not done. The pad already carries the fire button the seats reuse as a trigger, and the strip already carries TANK, GUNSHIP and SOL-82.
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --phone — PASS phone-opening, phone-skip-run, phone-drive, phone-build, phone-gunship-briefing, phone-gunship-seat, phone-nuke-release, phone-sol82, phone-debrief, phone-debrief-last, phone-sector-3, phone-landscape.

Found and fixed: the SKIP TUTORIAL card sat on the coach card's second line and ate the word 'or' (artifacts/browser/phone-opening.png); the gunship readout and the ground-truth monitor overlapped at 390 px and the seat panel's header ran under the radar (artifacts/browser/phone-gunship-seat.png); SOL-82's panel sat on the scope's PASS telemetry, which in portrait hangs under a lens drawn across the top; the LASER and SHIELD pad buttons were 42 px, under the thumb rule; the HUD's top: 46px predates the navigation shell's bar, whose row ends at 54.

The probe grew the two selectors that had let the first of those through: #td-tut was never in the chrome set, and the gunship seat's layout check measured its buttons but not its header or its map button.
Regression steps re-run green on this branch: --nav, --skip-tutorial, --defense, --gunship. npm test (120 programs) and npm run check green at each commit.

--laser-game fails at 'laser=online brings SOL-82 online' (state().laser.online is false). Reproduced with src/ and styles.css checked out from main in the same worktree, so it is not from this work; artifacts/browser/laser-game-load-failure.json.

Open, not fixed: in the gunship seat on a phone the ground-truth monitor's scissored render lands outside its framed box, so the frame reads empty and the render sits up and right of it (artifacts/browser/phone-gunship-seat.png). src/fx/story-monitor.js computes its viewport from the renderer canvas's client rect; the phone's canvas geometry is the suspect.
